Apple has released a new support document explaining how Spotlight indexing works on their devices, including three key points that Apple says can help the indexing process complete faster. Here are the details.

How to speed up the indexing process for the new Spotlight

As Apple prepares to roll out iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 and other operating systems announced at this year's WWDC, Apple has released a new support document containing tips to speed up the indexing process.

Essentially, this new indexing process builds and continuously maintains a searchable catalog stored on the device, allowing Spotlight and the new Siri AI to quickly find apps, files, messages, photos, contacts, settings and other content when users perform searches.

The index is stored locally on each device, meaning every Apple device a user owns must complete the indexing process separately.

Interestingly, Apple began laying the groundwork for this change as early as iOS 26.6. As we reported last month, Apple said that update would 'optimize Spotlight indexing to prepare for iOS 27,' meaning some of the indexing work is done ahead of the main software release.

Now, Apple has published a support article with practical tips to speed up indexing, particularly the initial indexing process — which can take some time for users with a large amount of data.

Here's what Apple has to say:

Depending on the amount of data on your device, Spotlight indexing may take several hours or even days. Subsequent incremental updates will be much faster. The indexing will complete faster under the following conditions: your device is not in use; your device is connected to power; and your device is connected to the internet over Wi-Fi or Ethernet, in case emails or other data need to be downloaded for indexing.

Apple adds that Mac users can check indexing progress via an indicator at the top of the Spotlight or Siri window (after pressing Command-Space). For iPhone, iPad and other devices, users may see a notification in the Settings app indicating that 'Search & Siri' is still being optimized.

Apple also mentions that Mail may display another notification while email indexing is still incomplete.
